flaky_rule: A test is flaky iff, across all recorded runs, it has >= 3 failures AND at least one pass in a run after its first failing run (intermittent — it recovered at least once). A test that starts failing and never passes again is a regression, not flaky.
note: Job templates the Manager can post for the QA triage department. Shape mirrors orchestrator/engine.py JOB_FAMILIES for TicketDesk (key, title, brief, budget_credits, acceptance_criteria). Each template's check is deterministic and implemented in checks.py; the Reviewer runs the check by re-reading QADesk state through the tool layer — no LLM judgement. 'target_run' = 'latest' means the most recent run in list_runs (the overnight run in the seeded dataset).

acceptance_criteria: Every failure in the target run has a cluster assignment (cluster_id set), and each assigned cluster's signature equals the failure's own error signature
templates.brief: Group every failure from the overnight CI run by its error signature using the cluster tool, so each failure belongs to exactly one signature cluster. Then leave a short triage note on each cluster summarising what it looks like.
templates.title: Cluster the overnight failures

acceptance_criteria: The set of quarantined tests is exactly the set of tests failing intermittently (>= 3 failures with at least one pass after the first failure) in the recorded history — none missing, none extra
templates.brief: Work out which tests are genuinely flaky from their recorded pass/fail history (failing intermittently — at least 3 failures with a pass after the first failure) and quarantine exactly those tests. Consistent regressions and one-off failures must NOT be quarantined; they are real signal.
templates.title: Quarantine the flaky tests

acceptance_criteria: A regression verdict is recorded for the target run and is consistent with its new-failure count ('regression' iff new-failure count > 0, else 'no_regression')
templates.brief: Decide whether the overnight CI run introduced a regression: compare its failures' error signatures against all earlier runs, count the failures whose signature is brand-new in this run, record the verdict with the verdict tool, and leave a triage note on the run explaining the call.
templates.title: Regression verdict for the overnight run

verdict_rule: A run's only consistent regression verdict is 'regression' iff its new_failure_count > 0 (failures whose error signature was first seen in that run), otherwise 'no_regression'.
